rules.feed_seq: scope-wide, strictly increasing, one per status write in the scope; unsigned feed metadata
rules.full_feed: GET /v1/scopes/{scope}/status: the latest record of every version in the scope, ordered by feed_seq; the reply's feed_seq is the scope's current one
rules.after: ?after=N: only versions whose latest record has feed_seq > N; 410 feed_after_unavailable when N is above the current feed_seq or below the oldest point the registry serves; 200 with no records when nothing is newer
rules.client: keep the highest feed_seq applied per scope and the highest status sequence per version; a lower feed_seq, a lower sequence, or the same sequence with other bytes is feed_rollback; advance feed_seq only when every record applied or was a duplicate; first fetch, feed_rollback and feed_after_unavailable in an incremental poll fall back to the full feed

views.name: full_at_5
views.note: the default: latest record of every version

views.name: nothing_newer
views.note: 200 with no records and the current feed_seq, never 304 (304 answers only If-None-Match)

views.name: after_above_current
views.note: a stale edge copy or a registry rollback; the registry does not tell them apart

views.name: after_below_kept_history
views.note: this registry serves ?after= only from 2 on

views.name: after_5_at_7
views.note: f2 (feed_seq 6) is skipped: f3 is the flow version's latest record

client_cases.name: first_fetch_is_full
client_cases.note: no feed_seq held for the scope yet, so the client fetches the full feed

client_cases.name: feed_seq_rollback_incremental
client_cases.note: a stale copy answers with feed_seq 5 after the client applied 7: refused, nothing applied, fall back to the full feed

client_cases.name: feed_seq_rollback_full
client_cases.note: the full feed itself is behind: refused and logged; the client keeps what it holds

client_cases.name: record_rollback
client_cases.note: a reply whose feed_seq is newer but which carries a lower status sequence than the one applied (s2 after s3)
